clues.text: This city stands on a thumb of land that juts into a broad harbor. The sea wraps it on most sides, past bays and inlets.
clues.narrowing: Rules out inland towns; puts the player on a harbor peninsula on the Atlantic coast.

source.quote: Boston was founded on Shawmut Peninsula in 1630

clues.text: Cold sea storms, called nor'easters, can bury this coast town in snow. Winters are cold and stormy, with spells of heavy snow and rain.
clues.narrowing: Rules out mild coasts; keeps a stormy coast where sea storms dump snow and rain.

source.quote: Boston's coastal location on the North Atlantic makes the city very prone to nor'easters , which can produce large amounts of snow and rain

clues.text: Puritan settlers crossed to this shore in 1630 and founded the town. A pact one year before had set up their bay colony, led by its first governor.
clues.narrowing: Shrinks the list to towns founded in 1630 as the seat of a Puritan bay colony.

source.quote: which created the Massachusetts Bay Colony and was signed by the colony's first governor, John Winthrop

clues.text: In 1773, angry townsfolk threw a whole shipment of tea into the harbor. They fought a tax they hated, and the act fired up a revolution.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: one harbor, one tea shipment, dumped in 1773 to fight a tax.

source.quote: In 1773, a group of angered Bostonian citizens threw a shipment of tea by the East India Company into Boston Harbor in protest of the Tea Act

clues.text: The laws of Massachusetts are made in this city. It is the state capital, and the state's largest city too.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: the state capital, and biggest city of the state, is this one.

source.quote: is the capital and most populous city of the U.S. state of Massachusetts

reveal.blurb: Puritan settlers founded Boston on a peninsula in 1630, and in 1773 its people dumped tea in the harbor to fight a tax. Today it stands as a great port and learning center on the Atlantic coast. Boston is the capital of Massachusetts.
